## Summary
John, your performance has shown some improvement over the last few weeks, particularly with your total hours billed in the week of May 16-22, where you achieved 26.5 hours. However, the recent week from May 23-29 was a significant dip, with only 17.7 hours logged and no repair orders billed. Let's focus on converting your available jobs into productive hours this week! 

## What's Working
- You achieved 26.5 hours in the week of May 16-22, which is a solid 55.8% of your goal. This shows you can reach your targets when you have assignments.
- On Thursday, May 18, you logged 10.6 hours, which indicates your ability to maximize productivity on busy days. 💪
- Your consistent attendance throughout the week has been commendable, especially on days like Monday and Tuesday when you logged hours even without ROs.

## Where to Focus
- The recent week (May 23-29) saw a drop to only 17.7 hours, which is just 20.4% of your goal. This is a concern as it impacts your overall productivity and potential earnings. Aim to actively pick up jobs from the shared queue to improve this.
- There are currently **no open ROs** assigned to you, which is a missed opportunity. Having active work will not only increase your hours but also help you stay engaged. Make it a priority to select jobs from the queue.
- The jobs awaiting assignment include several that are aging, such as RO 777988 (Check Engine Light) and RO 777947 (Metal Shavings in Oil). Addressing these sooner rather than later will help you accumulate hours and improve your performance metrics. 📈
- Focus on converting your available time into billable hours. For example, you logged only 5.2 hours on Tuesday, May 16, which could have been higher if you had picked up an additional RO.

## Action Items for This Week
1. Select at least **two jobs** from the shared queue to work on this week, starting with RO 777988 and RO 777947.
2. Aim to log at least **30 hours** this week by maximizing your time on the floor and ensuring you are working on billable tasks.
3. Check in daily with your service advisor to stay updated on any new ROs that come in, ensuring you have a steady flow of work. 

## WIP Watchlist
- Nothing critical — keep moving. Ensure you are proactive in picking up jobs from the queue to avoid a backlog.
